title: [Feature] Enable prefix caching for GLM KDA RecoverSSM
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Allow GLM KDA RecoverSSM to use prefix caching with Mamba cache mode `align`. Previously configuration validation rejected prefix caching, and the inherited MRV2 KDA builder required physical state indices that Ascend did not prepare.

Prepare those indices with the same device-independent helper used by Ascend GDN before calling the upstream KDA builder. Reuse the existing accepted-state recovery and block-boundary checkpoint kernels. Update the serving guide and extend the four-card regression to check cache hits and identical cold/warm token outputs in eager and graph modes.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Experimental GLM KDA RecoverSSM can now run with `--enable-prefix-caching`; vLLM selects Mamba cache mode `align` automatically. Disabling prefix caching continues to use mode `none`. Other execution restrictions remain unchanged.

### How was this patch tested?

1. Configuration, metadata, cache-layout, KDA-contract and scheduler CPU regressions: 89 passed. State-index cases cover block boundaries, changing sequence positions, padded graph rows and unchanged source block tables.
2. A3 hardware (`80.5.9.129`, Ascend 9392): 12 RecoverSSM align-operator reference tests passed. The four-card W8A8 synthetic Flash regression passed with prefix caching enabled in eager and FULL_DECODE_ONLY graph modes, checking nonzero prefix hits and identical cold/warm output tokens.
3. Real GLM-5.3-Flash W8A8 on the same A3, TP8 + EP, BF16 model dtype/KV cache, MTP5, FULL_DECODE_ONLY: 30 GSM8K questions with prefix caching disabled and enabled. Accuracy was 28/30 with caching disabled, 28/30 with an empty enabled cache and 28/30 on warm repeats; the same two questions were incorrect in all three runs. All 30 cold/warm token sequences matched exactly; every warm request hit at least 1280 cached tokens (640-token blocks). Generating a different suffix against a shared prefix left the original request's output unchanged. Disabled/enabled cold token sequences matched in only 2/30 cases. One final numeric answer differed between the disabled and enabled runs; both answers were incorrect. These results establish the observed accuracy and cache-reuse behavior on this sample, not token equivalence between cache modes.
4. vLLM source was aligned to the repository-verified main commit; effective Triton Ascend was 3.2.2. Ruff, Ruff formatting, Markdownlint, Codespell and `git diff --check` passed. Full `bash format.sh ci` was attempted, but actionlint environment installation failed with a network disconnect.
5. A5 align-operator tests passed (12 cases). A5 end-to-end validation remains pending: its first run exited before model initialization because another workload consumed the devices. This draft primarily provides the completed A3 validation; no A5 end-to-end success is claimed.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542
